clue.text: Most of the merchant fleet in ancient Greece

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its final letter is kept here

parts.note: an argosy is a fleet of large merchant ships

explanation.surface: A remark that ancient Greek shipping was dominated by one trading fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops the last letter Y from ARGOSY. Homer often uses the city name for the whole of Greece, which makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer the city-state of the Argives stands for the whole Greek homeland, so its name serves for ancient Greece.

clue.text: Economist's so-called allegory of the first man

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition reads 'Economist is'

indicators.note: so-called means the following phrase is called out, so it is judged by its spoken sound

parts.note: the first man is Adam, and an allegory about him is Adam's myth

explanation.surface: An economist's own work is dismissed as a fable about Adam.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Economist's' stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish author of The Wealth of Nations is the founding figure of classical economics.

clue.text: Very lightweight character

definitions.meaning: the smallest unit in the old troy and avoirdupois weight systems, about 65 milligrams
the inherent nature or texture of something, as in going against the run of it

explanation.surface: A description of a slight, insignificant person.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiny weight unit is very light; the word also means temperament or texture, as in 'against the grain'.

clue.text: Part of breastwork disinterred from Munster

indicators.note: disinterred means dug up and disturbed, so these letters are turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: Part of a military earthwork excavated in the Irish province of Munster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breastwork' suggests a fortification, but here it means the work of the chest's bones; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The breastbone is the flat bone at the front of the chest, a part of the body's frame there.

clue.text: Mad Saudi fell in hail of bullets

indicators.note: mad means crazy or disordered, so the letters of the next two words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A crazed Saudi gunman is cut down by gunfire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' rearranges SAUDI and FELL together; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A volley of shots fired together or in rapid succession is a burst of gunfire.

clue.text: Said to be florid — and covered in powder!

indicators.note: said to be means the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: florid prose is flowery, over-ornate

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone's speech is overblown, and dusty too.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dusted with milled grain is white and powdery, like a baker's hands.

clue.text: Film plot in which coins are forged

indicators.note: forged means hammered into new shape, so the letters of the two words are refashioned

explanation.surface: A heist movie in which counterfeit money drives the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forged' rearranges COINS and ARE; 'in which' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A screenplay outline or storyline sketched out for a movie.

clue.text: Divine rebel and former striker

definitions.meaning: the angel who rebelled against God and was cast out of heaven
an old name for a friction match, struck to light it

explanation.surface: A description of an angel who was once a strike leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker' suggests a footballer or a worker on strike; it is a match that is struck.
explanation.definitionFit: Satan's name before his fall is also the old brand-name for an early friction match.

clue.text: Attacked Paul's predecessor instead, perhaps

parts.note: Paul the apostle was earlier called Saul, a persecutor of Christians; acting as that earlier self rather than as Paul would be to attack

explanation.surface: Someone set upon the man who came before Paul in a job.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as AS SAUL-TED: behaved as Saul (Paul's name before his conversion, when he hunted Christians) instead of as Paul. 'Attacked' is the plain meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: To set upon someone violently is to make a physical attack on them.

clue.text: Pass required by the school leaver

definitions.text: Pass required by the school leaver

parts.words: Pass required by the school leaver
parts.note: not a pupil leaving for good, but a boarder going home for a weekend, who needs a permit

explanation.surface: A school-leaver needs a pass in an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School leaver' suggests someone finishing education and 'pass' an exam result; it is a boarding pupil's leave of absence.
explanation.definitionFit: In British boarding schools this Latin word ('let him go out') names permission for temporary absence.

clue.text: Charity day an eye-opener in this abode of free love!

parts.note: agape is the Greek word for selfless Christian love, rendered 'charity' in older Bibles
Mon is the short form of Monday

indicators.note: an opener is what starts something, so the first letter of the word eye is taken

explanation.surface: Love of one's neighbour proves a revelation in a hippie commune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eye-opener' looks like a revelation but gives the opening letter E of 'eye'; 'an' is a link. The answer was a notorious Victorian religious commune in Somerset.
explanation.definitionFit: The name, Greek for 'abode of love', was given to a Victorian Somerset sect's house famed for scandal.

clue.text: Dismiss English class

parts.note: to cast out or cast aside is to dismiss

explanation.surface: An instruction to send away a group of English pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: A hereditary social rank, especially in Hindu society, is a fixed class.

clue.text: Origin of subversive movements in the Rockies? No, in California

definitions.text: Origin of subversive movements in the Rockies? No, in California

parts.words: Origin of subversive movements in the Rockies? No, in California
parts.note: the subversive movements are underground shifts of rock, earthquakes, and the rocks are not the Rocky Mountains but Californian bedrock

explanation.surface: A question about where a revolutionary political movement began in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subversive movements' suggests politics; read it as movements from below the surface, quakes along the great Californian geological rift.
explanation.definitionFit: The great transform boundary between the Pacific and North American plates runs through California and causes its earthquakes.

clue.text: One sort of officer with a state salary

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
NCO is a non-commissioned officer, such as a sergeant
ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine

explanation.surface: A kind of officer who is paid by the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings from employment are the money a person receives, of which pay is the main part.

clue.text: Detach oneself-the company's getting lewd

parts.note: the company of actors in a play is its cast; the 's is 'is'
loose as in loose morals means promiscuous or lewd

explanation.surface: A remark that the theatre troupe is turning bawdy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link here; the possessive in 'company's' adds no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten a boat's line and drift free is a phrase for separating oneself from ties.

clue.text: Loftier Greek from the mouth of the priesthood

indicators.note: words that come from the mouth are spoken, so the sound of the phrase counts

parts.note: loftier is higher, and Attic is the Greek dialect of Athens

explanation.surface: A grand Greek utterance comes from a priest's lips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the mouth of' looks like part of the definition, but 'from the mouth' signals the sound; 'of the priesthood' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things belonging to priests, notably the cursive script used by Egyptian priests.

clue.text: Poor Racine got the wind up, finding one in bed

indicators.note: poor means badly made, so the letters of the dramatist's name are rearranged
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: air is moving wind or breeze

explanation.surface: A nervous French playwright discovers a woman in his bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' gives CINERA from RACINE; 'up' turns AIR into RIA. 'got' and 'finding' are links; 'bed' is a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: This daisy-like pot and garden plant is grown in flower beds and borders.

clue.text: Snatch and grab, in the sailor's case

parts.note: a snatch of song is a ditty, a short simple tune
to bag something is to grab or seize it

explanation.surface: A theft and robbery involving a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snatch and grab' looks like a robbery; 'snatch' is a fragment of song. 'and' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaman's small bag for sewing kit, needles and personal odds and ends.

clue.text: Henry I's terror of the Spanish

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
I's gives the letters I and S as written
panic is sudden overwhelming terror

explanation.surface: A Tudor king's fear of Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Henry I of England; it splits into H, I'S and PANIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to Spain or Spanish-speaking peoples and lands.

clue.text: One more place in the team to be filled

definitions.meaning: an additional one, a further example

definitions.text: place in the team to be filled
definitions.meaning: ... is the stand-in name printed on a team sheet for a player yet to be chosen

explanation.surface: A team still has one more vacancy to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: On British team sheets, 'A. N. Other' marks a place not yet allocated to a named player.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an additional one, and split up it is the placeholder name for an unnamed team member.

clue.text: Boat with hideaway for a tomboy

parts.note: a hoy is a small coasting vessel
a den is a secret retreat or hideaway

explanation.surface: A girl with a secret boat hideout plays like a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a boisterous, high-spirited girl.

clue.text: Underground supervisor, a Nietzchean figure

definitions.meaning: a foreman in a mine, overseeing work below ground
an early English rendering of Nietzsche's Übermensch, the superior human

explanation.surface: A mine foreman who resembles a figure from Nietzsche's philosophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underground' suggests a spy or the Tube; here it is a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: A mine foreman bears this title, which also translated Nietzsche's ideal superior human before 'superman' prevailed.

clue.text: Jumbo pilot on top of his job

definitions.text: Jumbo pilot on top of his job

parts.words: Jumbo pilot on top of his job
parts.note: not an airline captain of a jumbo jet but a driver who sits literally on top of an elephant

explanation.surface: An airline captain flying a jumbo jet is very competent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbo pilot' suggests a jumbo jet; 'on top of his job' is literal: he sits on the elephant he works with.
explanation.definitionFit: In India and South-East Asia, an elephant's keeper and driver rides on its neck.

clue.text: Pinky the salesman is after a customer

indicators.note: after places the salesman's word behind the customer's word in the answer

parts.note: a customer can mean a chap or fellow, as in 'an awkward customer'
a commercial traveller is a travelling salesman

explanation.surface: A rosy-cheeked sales rep is chasing a client.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinky' looks like a nickname; it is slang for a left-wing sympathiser. 'is' and 'a' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A Communist sympathiser who is not a party member was called a pink or pinko.

clue.text: Filly expert in Animal Farm, for example

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for filly in horse-racing form
able means skilled or expert

explanation.surface: A young mare excels on Orwell's Animal Farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's story of talking farm animals is an allegorical tale with a moral.

clue.text: Fancies fellows

definitions.meaning: fancies as a verb means is fond of
the plural noun means equals or similar people

explanation.surface: A remark that someone is attracted to men.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means enjoys or favours, and the plural noun means people of the same kind.

clue.text: Cubicle in footwear fashion centre

parts.note: a boot is an item of footwear

indicators.note: centre means the middle letter of the word fashion is taken

explanation.surface: A changing cubicle in a shoe boutique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A small enclosed compartment, as for voting or telephoning.

clue.text: Job, perhaps, for one in the ring

definitions.meaning: the Book of Job is one book of the Bible, so its author is a writer of a book
a bookie taking bets in the betting ring at a racecourse

explanation.surface: A job opening for a boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Job' at the start hides its capital: it is the biblical book. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookie takes bets at the racecourse, and split it names a maker of a book, like the biblical one.

clue.text: The soldier's head may be turned by such words

definitions.text: The soldier's head may be turned by such words

parts.words: The soldier's head may be turned by such words
parts.note: not flattery that turns a soldier's head, but a parade command on which troops turn their heads to one side

explanation.surface: A soldier might be swayed by flattering words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head may be turned' suggests vanity; literally, on this drill order soldiers snap their heads to the right.
explanation.definitionFit: The parade-ground command makes marching troops look to the right in salute.

clue.text: Settle down with a girl

parts.note: to nest is to settle in a home

explanation.surface: A man settles down with his girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, a Welsh pet form of Agnes.
